description: Automerge is the default posture here, not the exception. This repo is a design catalog with no downstream consumers: nothing depends on its artifacts, so a bad bump costs a revert, not a broken release. What stops a bad bump reaching main is the `Protect Main` ruleset — CI (build + discovery, unit tests, ktfmtCheck, catalog spec, catalog spec) is required, and `platformAutomerge` hands the merge to GitHub's own auto-merge, which only fires once those checks pass. Set the ruleset up with `scripts/setup-repo-protection.sh`; without it, automerge silently degrades to merging as soon as Renovate can, which is not what any of this intends.

packageRules.description: Majors are never automerged. A major on Kotlin, Compose Multiplatform or the preview toolchain changes what the catalog renders, and the render is the product — a human looks at the visual diff before it lands. Also hold a major for two weeks so the ecosystem's first round of regressions surfaces on someone else's CI.
Wear Compose and the mobile Compose BOM decide how every sticker in the catalog is laid out, and the render is the product — so they land as one PR whose visual diff is the review, not on automerge.

Horologist is the catalog's SECOND component library (see AGENTS.md) and it ships its artifacts as one release — media-ui-material3, auth-composables-material3, compose-layout, images-base and the models they take all move together, and a skew between them is a compile error at best. Group them into one PR. Not automerged, for the same reason Compose is not: these draw the media player, the sign-in screens and the fast-scrolling list, and the render is the product — a human reads the visual diff. They are on an alpha line, so expect the diff to be real.

Toolchain and CI plumbing — the Gradle wrapper, the GitHub Actions pins and the pinned Node version. These are judged entirely by whether CI passes, which is the one thing automerge already waits for, so batch them into a single weekly PR rather than one PR per action. Deliberately BEFORE the compose-ai-tools rule, which re-claims its own action ref out of this batch — that pin travels with the Gradle coords, not with the weekly plumbing.

LAST ON PURPOSE. Renovate applies packageRules in order and the LAST match wins, so while this rule sat above the CI-toolchain rule the pinned `compose-ai-tools` action ref — a github-actions dependency — was pulled back out of this group into the weekly batch, and the two halves of one release drifted apart exactly as the rule below says they must not (compose-ai-tools#4220 found the pin three releases behind the Gradle coords). Keep this rule below the CI-toolchain one; the only rule allowed after it is the rc-players rule that follows, which exists to take one package back out of this group. compose-ai-tools ships the preview CLI, the ee.schimke.composeai Gradle artifacts (the preview-annotations dependency and the ee.schimke.composeai.preview plugin marker) and the reusable CI actions/workflows as a single release. Group the pinned action refs and the Gradle coords into ONE PR so the CLI, plugin and annotation pins can never skew apart — a skew breaks preview discovery outright. Track it aggressively and automerge once CI is green: the release moves several times a day and the pin is only useful if it keeps up. Republishing the catalog against the new renderer needs no extra step, because design-artifacts.yml has a push trigger on main covering the manifest paths this PR touches.

AFTER the compose-ai-tools rule, and the only thing allowed to sit there: the last match wins, so this rule takes `third-party-rc-embedded-player` back out of that group. It carries the ee.schimke.composeai GROUP, but it is not part of that release — it is published from yschimke/rc-players on a version line of its own that is already ahead. Grouped, Renovate raised the shared `composePreviewAnnotations` ref to a player-only version and dragged four compose-ai-tools artifacts to a version nobody published, which is what broke #199. Ungrouped it moves on its own ref (`rcEmbeddedPlayer` in gradle/libs.versions.toml) in a PR of its own. Automerged like its neighbour and for the same reason: the connector resolves the player's entry point reflectively, so a skew shows up as the embedded lane going quiet, and the render CI is what catches that.
